faq.q: How cold does it get where emperor penguins breed?
faq.a: Emperor penguins breed on Antarctic sea ice in winter, when the air can drop to minus 40 degrees Celsius and strong winds make it feel even colder. No other bird breeds in such cold.
asks: How do penguins survive the Antarctic winter?

faq.q: How do penguin fathers survive winter without eating?
faq.a: Males live on their body fat while they guard the egg for about two months, and in all they may fast for nearly four months and lose close to half their weight. Huddling helps the fat last.
asks: Why do penguin dads not eat?
How long do male emperor penguins fast?

faq.q: How warm is it inside a penguin huddle?
faq.a: In a tightly packed huddle the temperature can rise above 30 degrees Celsius, sometimes even near body temperature, while the air outside is far below freezing.
asks: Is it warm in the middle of a huddle?

faq.q: How do penguins take turns in a huddle?
faq.a: Every 30 to 60 seconds the huddle moves in a wave of tiny steps. Over time this slowly rotates birds between the windy edge and the warm centre, so no penguin is left out in the cold for long.
asks: Do penguins swap places in a huddle?

faq.q: Where does a penguin keep its egg?
faq.a: An emperor penguin keeps its egg on top of its feet, covered by a warm fold of feathered skin called a brood pouch, so the egg never touches the ice.
asks: Why do penguins hold eggs on their feet?

facts: Emperor penguins are the only birds that breed during the Antarctic winter.
Studies have measured temperatures above 30 degrees Celsius inside tight emperor penguin huddles.
